title: GEO: Generative Engine Optimization

problem.claim: Content creators have little to no control over when and how their content is displayed in generative engine responses.

gap.claim: A framework is needed to help content creators improve visibility in generative engine responses while accounting for the black-box and fast-moving nature of these engines.

contributions.claim: Generative Engine Optimization is introduced as a flexible black-box optimization framework for defining visibility metrics and improving content visibility in generative engine responses.
GEO-bench is introduced as a large-scale benchmark of diverse user queries across multiple domains with relevant web sources.
The effectiveness of GEO strategies varies across domains.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors describe GEO as the first novel paradigm for improving content visibility in generative engine responses.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that GEO can boost visibility by up to 40% in generative engine responses.
The authors report rigorous evaluation of GEO.
The authors report that GEO strategies have differing efficacy across domains.

narrative_sequence.summary: Generative engines use large language models to synthesize and summarize information from multiple sources in response to queries.
The shift toward generative engines creates a challenge for content creators because they have little control over content display.
The work introduces GEO as a black-box optimization framework for improving visibility and defining visibility metrics.
The work introduces GEO-bench to support systematic evaluation across diverse domains and queries.
The authors report visibility gains of up to 40% and domain-dependent strategy effectiveness.

source_observation.claim: Reported GEO strategy efficacy varies across domains.

interpretation.claim: Optimization strategies may need to account for domain-specific characteristics.

application.claim: Evaluate and tune visibility optimization methods separately across relevant domains.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish which domains require distinct methods or whether domain-specific tuning always improves outcomes.

source_observation.claim: Generative engines synthesize information from multiple sources and summarize it using large language models.

interpretation.claim: Content visibility depends on how generative systems select and synthesize information from sources.

application.claim: Design visibility interventions for black-box, synthesis-based retrieval environments.

exception.claim: The abstract does not specify the mechanisms by which generative engines select, weight, or display content.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the GEO optimization algorithms or visibility metrics.
The abstract does not identify the domains, queries, baselines, or evaluation protocol used in GEO-bench.
The abstract does not provide the distribution of visibility gains or statistical details.
The abstract does not report limitations, computational costs, or failure cases.
